content: Do not store this medication in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. When the product is expired or no longer needed, dispose of it properly according to local regulations. The information provided here was last updated in May 2024. Important Note on Usage of This Information: This document is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Uses: Levonorgestrel is used by women to prevent pregnancy after a failure of birth control methods (e.g., a broken condom) or after unprotected sexual intercourse. This medication may be less effective in women who weigh more than 164 pounds (74 kilograms) or if certain other medications have been used within the past month. Reduced effectiveness can result in pregnancy. Always check the ingredients on the label, even if you have used the product before, as manufacturers may change the formulation. Additionally, products with similar names may contain different ingredients intended for other purposes. How to Use: If you are using an over-the-counter product for self-treatment, carefully read all instructions on the product packaging before taking this medication. If you have any questions, consult your pharmacist. Take one tablet orally, with or without food, as soon as possible after unprotected intercourse. After taking this medication, the timing and flow of your menstrual period may change. Notify your doctor immediately if your period is more than seven days late. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, fatigue, dizziness, changes in vaginal bleeding, breast tenderness, or headache. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Precautions: Before taking levonorgestrel, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other progestins (e.g., norethindrone), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. While it passes into breast milk, it is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain drugs may reduce the effectiveness of emergency contraception by decreasing the levels of birth control hormones in your body, potentially leading to pregnancy. Examples include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), St. John’s wort, drugs used to treat seizures (e.g., barbiturates, carbamazepine, felbamate, phenytoin, primidone, topiramate), and certain HIV medications (e.g., nelfinavir, nevirapine), among others. Overdose: An overdose of this medication is highly unlikely. However, if someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. The information provided here was last revised in May 2024.
